title: vLLM-Ascend packaging metadata and CPU test shims prove different things
mechanism: At vLLM-Ascend revision 175ef4d49c2072f9233619636f0309f4f88b4e2c, setup.py declares platform, general-plugin and service-metric entry points. These strings are distribution metadata; the loader and registration function bodies are outside this source unit. When SOC_VERSION is empty, setup.py queries npu-smi to determine the build target. A missing executable returns an empty chip string and triggers the CPU-only guidance, whereas a non-zero command becomes a separate RuntimeError. tests/ut/conftest.py uses a different npu-smi info probe. Failure installs CPU mocks, including torch.npu.is_available=False. Independently of that probe result, setdefault inserts synthetic A2 build information when vllm_ascend._build_info is absent, and adapt_patch plus custom-op registration subsequently run. Successful unit-test setup therefore does not by itself prove a real device was selected, that native extensions built, or that an entry-point loader executed.
corrections: Do not merge npu-smi command failure with executable absence.
The build-info setdefault is outside the failed-probe branch.
Entry-point metadata and test imports are not device acceptance evidence.
source_scope: Root accepted only the rewritten mechanism. Independent Cursor reading and its broader findings remain in the immutable author packet. Root source reading is enumerated separately.
adoption_boundary: Use to diagnose packaging and test-environment differences. Native build, loader execution and device behavior require their own observed results.
